By offering coconut water, one obtains the fruit of the Vahniṣṭoma sacrifice. || 294 ||
One who offers grains mixed with honey and parched rice.
And by [giving] the finest barley-meals, one obtains the Vahniṣṭoma sacrifice.
One who offers vegetables shall obtain the merit associated with the forest-dweller (vānaprastha).
And by giving a *harītaka* fruit, one shall obtain that very same fruit. || 296 ||
One who offers bulbs and roots shall obtain birth in a good family.
Likewise, O twice-born ones, [the fruits] of the blue lotus, the vidārī, and the tarūṭa; || 297 ||
By giving a water-pot, one obtains the fruit of the forest-dweller's stage of life.
By giving tin and cāruka, one obtains the fruit of the white lotus. || 298 ||
Having given karkandhu, badara, as well as pālevata and dhava;
Likewise, the *pārūṣaka*, the *panasa*, and the *nārikela* have been described. || 299 ||
The bhavya, mocā, and aucca fruits, as well as the date and the pomegranate.
And among the mangoes and other fruits, there are those produced from the *akṣoṭa*, *māranāla*, and *priyālu* trees.
Jāmbū, bilva, āmala, as well as jāti, śrī, and nāruka.
And the orange, the citron, and also the fruits of the rājaphalgu tree. || 301 ||
Likewise, one should offer even insignificant things as primary offerings with devotion to the God of gods.
And whoever bestows these and other such fruits as well. ||302||
One attains the fruitfulness of one's actions, as well as the heavenly world.
The udumbara, the kapittha, and likewise that which is the dantaśaṭha. || 303 ||
Such things as these should never be given to a deity.
The one who offers a grape obtains strength and health. ||304||
One obtains the primary flavors as well as supreme good fortune.
By worshipping the Lord of Gods with mangoes, one obtains the fruit of a horse sacrifice. || 305 ||
Having offered betel nuts and nutmegs, as well as clove leaves in the same manner.
Then cardamom, kaṅkola, cardamom (melā), and likewise katuphala. || 306 ||
By [giving] a sprout of betel vines, one shall attain the heavenly world.
The highest good fortune in the world, as well as unsurpassed beauty. || 307 ||
By giving mouth-perfume, one shall become beloved by women.
And by the giving of measures [of grain], one does not go to hell at all. || 308 ||
One should fill the vessels with foods and edibles; if these are unavailable, one should do so with other suitable items.
Whatever one offers to the God of gods while endowed with devotion, [that is accepted]. || 309 ||
He attains that very same inexhaustible merit and goes to the heavenly world.
The god does not attain satisfaction through abundant accumulations of wealth.
Just as He who is dear to His devotees attains satisfaction through devotion.
Through devotion one attains desires; through devotion one goes to heaven. || 311 ||
Through devotion one attains that state, having gone to which one does not grieve.
For that which is given with ordinary devotion is indeed returned by means of one's feet.
O best among the foremost of the twice-born, [they approached him] with single-minded devotion, bowing their heads.
With a pair of white garments as well as auspicious pearls. || 313 ||
With the primary incense of camphor, with milk, and with milk-rice (pāyasa).
And also with a wick made from a lotus fiber and with incense of ghee. || 314 ||
Worshipping her while remaining entirely pure, one becomes auspicious and the bestower of all desires.
Having performed this, the sick person is swiftly and without doubt liberated from disease. ||315||
One afflicted by suffering is released from suffering; one who is bound is released from bondage.
And just as one seized by a king may be released, so too may a man be freed from the fear of a king. || 316 ||
In this way, one may travel the road safely, avoiding all misfortune.
One should bathe the deity with oil and then anoint him with saffron.
A person should worship with red garments and likewise with corals.
And with bandhujīvaka flowers and incense produced from agaru. || 316 ||
With a lamp of oil and a wick dyed with great red lac.
Along with grape juice, cakes, and kṛsara. || 319 ||
One should worship her who is entirely red; she brings about the destruction of the enemy faction.
She is the producer of good fortune in the world and the increaser of wealth and grain.
It bestows heaven and grants fruits, and it brings men and women under one's control.
Thus, O twice-born ones, has the fruit of the gift of those characterized by passion been declared by me. ||321||
If one should offer anything whatsoever in a world characterized by sattva, even without desire.
By that very means, one attains the state where, having gone there, one does not grieve.
Those fools who recite the Dharma for the sake of gain are the lowest of men, desiring only rewards.
Those who place their trust in the Lord of the World then obtain all their desires.
But for those of small intelligence, their fruit is indeed finite.
O best of the twice-born, this is for those sattvic men who are without desire.
This too will certainly lead to liberation from all suffering.
The Blessed One Viṣṇu is infinite; [this applies] to him by those who are free from desire. || 325 ||
Whatever little is given, that alone is said to be inexhaustible.
The God accepts with his two feet what is offered by one who possesses desire.
O best of the twice-born, that which is given by one who lacks desire is accepted [by the recipient] upon his head.
Then, with food offerings, or with flowers, or with various accumulations of wealth.
There is no purpose for that omnipresent, immeasurable Self.
Out of devotion and for the sake of bestowing grace upon his devotees, he accepts what is given. || 328 ||
Therefore, in all circumstances, devotion alone is the cause here.
Having attained a state of solitude, they are free from all sensual desires. ||329||
Having attained the station of Viṣṇu, one shall never return again.
They have no fear of hell, nor any fear arising from disease.
Nor do those people who have taken refuge in Janārdana suffer from the enemy that is worldly existence.
Having offered with devotion that flower, even if it is difficult to obtain, to Madhusūdana;
O best of the twice-born, by offering even a blade of durva grass or water, one attains the worlds desired by the mind.

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-first chapter, titled "The Exposition on the Dharma of Giving," within the *Haṃsagītā* addressed to the sages, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the third section of the glorious *Viṣṇudharmottara*.
The sages said:
Salutations to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, Vāsudeva, Janārdana!
O compassionate one toward devotees, granter of boons, lotus-eyed one of noble vows! || 1 ||
O Brahman-like one, inconceivable person, you who cause the creation and destruction of the world!
O Lord of the three worlds, Govinda, you who are compassionate toward those who have come for refuge! || 2 ||
O Lord of all, O Sovereign who pervades all, O All-pervading One, homage be unto You!
Homage be to you, O Lord of the World, Sovereign of the lords of the worlds! || 3 ||
O Lord of Gods, remover of the affliction of liquor, you who are praised by Brahmā and Śiva!
O Viṣṇu, O Conqueror, O Hara, O Kṛṣṇa, O All-pervading One, whose eyes are the sun and the moon! || 4 ||
Resembling a thousand suns, you are intent upon the protection of the world.
O you who first appeared as the Boar and the Man-lion, O Vāmana of infinite prowess!
O Trivikrama, you who have stepped across the entire circumference of the cosmic egg with your strides!
O Lord of the hosts of enemies of the gods, all of whom have been struck down by the edge of your discus!
O you who cause the destruction of all obstacles through mere recollection!
Through this instruction of the Teacher, [the darkness] residing in our hearts has been destroyed.
O sinless one, you have blunted the power of all the weapons of the Dānavas in Vaikuṇṭha.
O You in whose belly the entire triad of worlds is contained! ||8||
O you who resemble a crescent moon, by whom the earth was lifted up with your tusks!
O Great Boar, who destroyed the great asura Hiraṇyākṣa!
O you whose sprout-like nails have been reddened by the blood from the chest of the lord of the Daityas!
O you who bear the form of Narasiṃha, encircled by garlands of flames!
O you whose form is variegated by the casting of Lakṣmī’s sidelong glances!
With his chest illuminated by the Kaustubha gem and wearing garments of gold.
Seated upon the seat of the serpent's coils, you whose preeminent banner is Tārkṣya.
O you who resemble a hundred moons, O seven-necked one, O knower of the Vedas! 12.
O you who increased the surface of the earth with the marrow from the destruction of Madhu and Kaiṭabha!
Salutations to you, the four-faced one born from the navel-lotus. ||13||
With hands and feet on all sides, with eyes, heads, and faces on all sides.
O Supreme Person, endowed with the excellence of all the senses, present everywhere! 14.
You are the supreme eye of yogins; you are the ultimate goal of yogins.
But yogins, having attained you, never turn back again. ||15||
Salutations to you, O God, from the front; salutations be to you from behind as well.
Homage be to you, O God, even as a beast; and homage be to you everywhere. 16.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus praised by those sages at that time, the sinless Blessed One—
He bestowed divine vision upon those sages of purified souls.
Then, he beheld the entire three worlds within his body.
Then [the sight] of Viṣṇu, who possesses immeasurable splendor and has assumed the form of a swan. 18.
Having seen the swan assuming a universal form, those whose wealth is austerity beheld that appearance.
Then, bowing with their heads, they went across the entire earth.
Then the God spoke to them all with a sweet voice.
He has a voice like the thundering of clouds and is the destroyer of the suffering of those who bow before him.
"Arise, O best of the twice-born, O sinless ones; choose a boon."
Having beheld Amoghadarśana, they obtained whatever their hearts desired.
The sages said:
Delusion is destroyed, memory is regained, and knowledge has been attained, O Janārdana.
You have been seen in your universal form; what need have we for any other boon?
Nevertheless, O Lord of Gods, if a boon is to be granted to us by you, [then grant it].
O Janārdana, may devotion toward you be ever-present and free from obstacles.
And this supreme dialogue of ours with you—
By reciting it, his liberation from all sins shall likewise come to pass.
From disease one becomes free from disease; from fear, one is freed from fear; and from bondage, one is released from bondage.
One who seeks dharma shall obtain dharma, and one who seeks wealth shall obtain wealth. ||25||
One who desires objects of pleasure shall obtain those pleasures; one who seeks liberation shall obtain liberation.
And the wise man who would retain this attains the supreme goal.
By hearing this scripture, one goes to the heavenly world.
It bestows wealth, fame, long life, and sons, and grants all desires. || 27 ||
May this scripture likewise be meritorious, O Slayer of Madhu.
Having heard this supreme scripture, which came into being through the grace of Viṣṇu. ||28||
This is the essence extracted even from the entirety of the scriptures, a testimony of the Supreme Person.
A man who has studied [this] for the best of the twice-born shall obtain his desired objects according to his heart's wish. || 29 ||

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-second chapter, titled "The Vision of the Universal Form of the Swan as Seen by the Sages," within the *Haṃsagītā* addressed to the sages, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, in the third section of the glorious *Viṣṇudharmottara*. The *Haṃsagītā* is complete.
Vajra said:
"The god Viṣṇu, the wide-striding one, is exceedingly easy to propitiate for those with a gracious countenance."
Being thus praised, he revealed his universal form to the twice-born.
Speak to my devotee regarding his supreme grace.
O Brahmana, I do not reach satiety while listening to this nectar of a story.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
O Great King, Mātali, the charioteer of Śakra, was an expert in the ritual procedure.
He has a daughter equal to him, renowned by the name Guṇakāśī.
In former times, both Mātali and Nārada went to search through that forest.
While they were walking about, [they saw] the grandson of the entire merchant's son.
Having seized the one named Sumukha, the two of them departed.
Then both of them requested Śakra from the Naga.
Śakra granted a boon to both Sumukha and Tārkṣya, granting them freedom from fear of one another.
Knowing the prowess of Tārkṣya, he went into the presence of Keśava.
The slayer of Madhu granted fearlessness to Sumukha and bestowed Tārkṣya upon him.
Then Tārkṣya, filled with wrath, approached Keśava.
Garuḍa said:
O Kṛṣṇa, why is this boon being granted to Sumukha while disregarding me?
Standing upon my back, you shall slay the enemies and be victorious.
You protect my enemy, who is a serpent that devours my family.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Having been addressed thus by him, Viṣṇu then spoke to Garuḍa.
"O Lord of Birds, you are not capable of carrying the entire world for me."
By my own self, I alone sustain myself in every battle.
If you have the power to carry it, bear one of my arms.
Having spoken thus, Hari placed his left arm upon his back.
Then, with a dejected face due to the abandonment of his wings, that best of birds—
Exhausted and dejected, he praised the Lord of Gods, the slayer of Madhu.
Garuḍa said:
Salutations to you, O Lord of the gods of gods, who are worshipped by both the Suras and the Asuras.
O invincible one, O lotus-eyed one, you who are affectionate toward those who have sought refuge!
I did not recognize your strength, for my mind was filled with self-conceit.
O sinless Lord, you alone always sustain the three worlds.
O Lord, you alone always carry yourself by means of yourself.
O God, within whose body the entire three worlds are situated. || 15 ||
For how could even thousands of those like me be able to carry it?
Therefore, O Blessed One, be gracious to me, who dwell beneath your banner.
O Lord of Gods, there is no end to your deeds within the three worlds.
Who is capable of recounting his deeds in their entirety? || 17 ||
Or even the mere recitation of your deeds—what praise could there be for you, O Supreme Lord?
You possess all powers everywhere; be gracious to me, O slayer of enemies!
O Vāsudeva, abode of all beings, Lord of the universe!
O Nārāyaṇa of great splendor, who reclines upon the ocean at the end of the eon!
Your body has been turned tawny by the filaments of the lotus at Your navel.
Be gracious to me; salutations to you, O bird who dwells upon the banner.
The Blessed One said:
O Tārkṣya, you should never harbor self-conceit.
I alone carry myself by my own self, and I also sustain you.
Your wife was not pleased by you, for you have indeed become one who has abandoned her side.
For your sake, I have placed the entire three worlds upon my arm.
For indeed, there is no one else in the world as powerful as you.
Whose life has not departed due to the touch of his staff-like arms. || 23 ||
O best of birds, having become powerful, you were born from my own body.
At the end of the fortnight, they will become distinguished; of this there is no doubt. || 24 ||
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Thus addressed, Suparṇa returned once more to the Suparṇas.
Or he obtained an increase in splendor and strength through the grace of the gods. || 25 ||
Thus, O Tārkṣya, being praised like a man, he [honored] the wielder of the Śārṅga bow.
Furthermore, he was restored to the state of Suparṇa and made exceedingly powerful.
By the mere request of Śakra, even Sumukha was made immortal.
Therefore, O King, understand this regarding that enemy of the Dānavas. ||27||
For there is indeed nothing that should not be given to devotees, even the sovereignty of the gods is certain [to be granted].
For those seized by the noose of death, there is likewise a falling into hell.
As soon as he was remembered, that Lord of Gods turned back out of fear of him.

O twice-born one, may the Slayer of Foes—who has destroyed all suffering for men who possess devotion, who is worthy of worship by the best of gods, who travels with the Lord of Birds (Garuḍa), and whose complexion has become lusterless—be pleased with you as you bow in devotion. Thus ends the three hundred and forty-third chapter, titled "The Description of the Story of Sumukha," in the third section of the *Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara*, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra.
Vajra said:
I desire to hear from you that which is indeed the supreme grace.
That powerful Viṣṇu has performed [this] for his devotees. ||1||
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
O King, in ancient times, Bali [conquered] Śakra in the three worlds.
Then Śakra went for refuge to Kaśyapa, his father.
Then Kaśyapa, taking Śakra with him, went to the Grandfather.
To him Brahmā, the giver of boons, said: "Go, Kaśyapa, to Keśava."
I seek refuge in the god Madhusūdana, who reclines upon the Ocean of Milk.
And request him for the status of a son; he shall become your son. ||4||
Then he will give the entire three worlds to the king of the gods.
And thus addressed, Kaśyapa, together with the leaders of the thirty [gods], [spoke].
Having gone there to the Ocean of Milk, he beheld Hari through his ascetic penance.
Having seen him, Hari then praised him with a hymn of praise.
The Lord, being pleased, assumed the form of a dwarf and became his son.
Having pervaded the entire three worlds with his three strides, the Sustainer of the Universe—
Having bound Bali, the lord of the Daityas, O Indra among kings, he gave him over to Śakra.
Having been thus praised by Kaśyapa, he indeed attained the status of being his son. ||8||
Vajra said:
With which hymn Kaśyapa praised Madhusūdana.
Relate that auspicious hymn which removes all sins.
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
Listen, O King, to this meritorious hymn proclaimed by Kaśyapa.
Having seen the God of gods risen from his bed upon the Ocean of Milk, [he approached him].
Kaśyapa said:

Oṃ, salutations to You, O God of gods, who are worshipped by the one-horned bull; O Sindhu-vṛkṣa, Vṛṣākapi, Lord of the gods, blameless one, auspicious one, Kapila, Viṣvaksena, Dhruva, Dharma, Banner of Dharma, Vaikuṇṭha, Vṛṣāvarta, You who are without beginning, middle, or end, Beloved of the people, scion of the Vṛṣṇis, You who recline upon the nectar, Eternal One, Abode of the three, Threefold Abode, Tuṣita, Dundubhi, [Lord] of the world of the great!

O Navel of the World, O Lotus-naveled One, O Viriñca, O Many-formed One, O Imperishable, O Consumer of Oblations, O Wielder of the Fragmented Axe, O You with a Circular Topknot, O Swan, O Greatly Generous One, O Lord of the Senses, O Subtle One, O Great Sage, O Praise-worthy One, O Stainless One, O Darkness, O Support of All Worlds, O Enveloped by Rays, O Passionless One, O First-born, O Son of Dharma, O Navel of Dharma, O Navel of Radiance, O Moon-charioted One, O Sinless One, You alone are the Dweller in the Ocean, O Unborn, O Single-footed One, O Thousand-fold Arrayed, O Great-headed One, O Thousand-eyed One, O Thousand-footed One, O Iron-faced One, O Great Person!

O thousand-armed one, O thousand-formed one, O thousand-eyed one, O source of a thousandfold power, those who know the Vedas call you the knower of the Vedas in a thousand ways. They say that you alone are the universality of all things; you are the flower-like smile, the supreme movement, the *vauṣaṭ* and the *vaṣaṭ* utterance, and the *svāhā* in sacrifices—you who consume the portions of the offerings. You are the hundred-streamed and the thousand-streamed; whether as *bhūḥ* or *bhuvaḥ*, you alone are the essence of Brahman. O Brāhmaṇeya, you are Brahmā; you are the quarters, you are the sky, you are the earth, you are Mātariśvan, and you are the Hotṛ, the Potṛ, the thinker, and the leader.

O foremost one, you alone are the cause of the oblation; through you as the abode of the universe, you are the quarters, the garland, the vessel, the one to be worshipped, the sustainer, and the one who has been worshipped. You alone are the refuge of the wise; you are yoga, you are liberation, you are the supreme, you are the sacrificial ladle, you are the creator, you are the sacrifice, you are Soma, you are the smoke, you are initiation, and you are the priestly fee. You are the universe, the ancient one, the conqueror of the powerful, O Hiraṇyagarbha, Nārāyaṇa, Ananta, Vṛṇasama, you who have the color of the sun, whose splendor is like the sun, O Great Person, Supreme Person, Primordial God, Lotus-navelled One, you of the lotus-smile.

O Lotus-dweller, lotus-eyed one, with golden-tipped hair, pure one, soul of the universe, god of the universe, facing all directions, trusty friend of all, source of all, consumer of all—you alone are the earth, the transcendent being, the maker of light, Śambhu, Bhava, the Self-born, the origin of beings, the great elements, the omnipresent, and the universe itself; you are the protector of the universe, you are the purifier, you are the oblation, O Creator of all! You are the upward-moving action, the foremost of immortality, the protector of the worlds, O Agni anointed with ghee! O Brahmā of infinite deeds, bring [him] under control; O you who are on every side, protect me, O Lord of the universe, from those seeking worldly boons! Thus [he prayed].
He who always composes hymns for the best of gods with the hymn fashioned by Kāśyapa.
Purified in the morning and with his mind fixed upon Him, he shall go to the worlds of the Supreme Person.

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-fourth chapter, titled "The Description of the Hymn to Kaśyapa," in the Dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra, within the third section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa. || 344 ||
Vajra said:
The supreme grace of that high-souled Keśava.
Speak to me, your devotee, concerning the God of gods, the wielder of the discus.
For I am not satiated by hearing that nectar of his words.
He alone in the world provides protection for the hands of men who are falling. || 2 ||
Mārkaṇḍeya said:
In ancient times, O sinless one, the gods and the sages were indeed disputing.
One should perform sacrifice with seeds that have been stored for at most three years. || 3 ||
Since seeds possess the consciousness of the unborn, you ought instead to kill a goat.
This was the position held by those seers of purified souls who were knowers of dharma.
But the bird of the gods was a winged creature; from that, it became the path traversed by birds.
There was a Vasu named Rājoparicara, the best among those who possess the earth.
Then the gods and the sages questioned the Vasu.
As it was said by Vasu in the past: "One should sacrifice with whatever has been brought forth."
For by means of speech that has gone toward falsehood, a king indeed sets in motion violence.
Having become one who constantly travels through the sky, he entered into a cavity in the earth.
Then, [there were those] dwelling in the cavities of the earth who spoke in favor of the faction of the gods.
The Dānavas set their minds upon the destruction of that devotee of the gods.
Having heard what they intended to do, the gods of swift prowess [acted].
And they reported the matter thus to Bṛhaspati, the preceptor of the gods.
Then Bṛhaspati, having gone there, [found] the king dwelling in a cavity of the earth.
He taught him the Vaiṣṇava protection-rite known as Aparājita.
By means of the recitations of deeds past, present, and future.
This knowledge was created by Brahmā; it brings about the destruction of all afflictions.
And having instructed that king, Bṛhaspati spoke as follows: || 11 ||
Bṛhaspati said:
Remaining here, O King, you shall enjoy the stream of wealth offered by the twice-born.
By the grace of the deities, he was also constantly nourished by her.
And by means of this knowledge, O King, you shall become invulnerable.
Even while stationed within a cavity of the earth, [he consumes] the Daityas, Dānavas, and Rākṣasas.
Having spoken thus to the king, he vanished right there.
Vajra said:
O best of the twice-born, tell me that protection which was indeed performed by the priest of the god.
For I consider that protection for King Vasu, while he remains within the depths of the earth, to be the foremost and supreme.

Thus ends the three hundred and forty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Protection of the King Residing in a Chasm," in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra within the third section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara Purāṇa. || 345 ||
Mārkaṇḍeya said:

Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed One, Vāsudeva; obeisance to Ananta, the thousand-headed one who reclines upon the ocean of milk, whose couch is the coils of Śeṣa, whose vehicle is Garuḍa; to the Unborn, the Unconquered, the one clad in yellow garments; O Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, Hayaśiras, Varāha, Narasiṃha, Vāmana, Trivikrama, Rāma, Rāma, Rāma—obeisance be to you, obeisance be to you, obeisance be to you!

Slay, slay! Cook, cook! Churn, churn! Destroy, destroy! Put to flight, put to flight! Reduce to ashes with your conch, discus, thunderbolt, mace, club, and plow—the Asuras, Varadas, Daityas, Dānavas, Yakṣas, Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Pretas, Piśācas, Kumbhāṇḍas, Siddhas, Yoginīs, Ḍākinīs, and the Grahas headed by Skanda, as well as the other planets and constellations! O Thousand-armed one, whose weapons and arms are a thousandfold, conquer, conquer! Be victorious, be victorious! O Unconquered One, whose gaze is unimpeded, blaze forth!

Blaze! Blaze forth! Blaze intensely! O you of universal form, of manifold forms, Madhusūdana, Mahāvarāha, Mahāpuruṣa, Vaikuṇṭha, Nārāyaṇa, Padmanābha, Govinda, Dāmodara, Hṛṣīkeśa, Keśava; O destroyer of all distress, bestower of sovereignty over all beings, shatterer of all evil dreams, breaker of all magical mechanisms, crusher of all serpents, Great Lord of all gods, liberator from all bonds, crusher of all enemies, destroyer of all fevers, warder-off of all planetary influences, pacifier of all sins, Janārdana—salutation be unto you, Svāhā!
Whoever recites, reads, hears, remembers, preserves, or proclaims this Aparājitā, the supreme Vaiṣṇavī, perfected Great Vidyā— for them there is no fear of fire, wind, thunderbolt,
stone, or lightning; no fear of the ocean, no fear of the planets, and no fear of thieves.

Or there shall be no fear of wild beasts; nor shall there be anywhere at night the fear of darkness, women, the royal court, hatred, poison, counter-poison, artificial poison, subjugation, incantations for causing enmity, or the fear of enmity, expulsion, killing, or imprisonment. By these recited mantras—accomplished, perfected, and worshipped—it is as follows:

Oṃ, homage be to you, O sinless one, unconquered, immeasurable, immortal, invincible, perfected by recitation, perfected by the mere thought of you, Ekānaṃśā, Umā, Dhruvā, Arundhatī, Sāvitrī, Gāyatrī, Jātavedasī, Mānastokā, Sarasvatī, Dharaṇī, Dhāraṇī, Saudāmanī, Aditi, Diti, Vinatā, Gaurī, Gāndhārī, Mātaṅgī, Kṛṣṇayaśodā, Satyavādinī, Brahmavādinī, Kālī, Kāpālī, Nidrā, O you who fulfill your promises! Thus ends the three hundred and fifty-first chapter, titled "The Narrative of the Universal Form," in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra within the third section of the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
Nara and Nārāyaṇa said:
At the very outset, in any delightful location—such as near a lake, a river, a spring, a house, a grove, or a mountain peak—one should prepare a well-levelled, charming mandala measuring one cubit.
Therein, one should draw an eight-petalled lotus in the center; then, one should divide it with the previously mentioned square and four-gated lines.
Then, in the middle of the lotus pericarp, one should meditate upon a white hundred-petalled lotus.

Above that pericarp is the solar disc (arka-maṇḍala), above that the lunar disc (candra-maṇḍala), and above that the fiery disc (agni-maṇḍala). In the center of that, one should place the Supreme Person (parama-puruṣa)—bodiless, odorless, tasteless, formless, touchless, soundless, all-pervading, ending in the prolated vowel (pluta), the syllable Om.

One should place the syllable *A* as Vāsudeva on the eastern petal of the lotus and meditate upon him as white in color; one should place the syllable *Ā* as Saṃkarṣaṇa on the southern [petal] and meditate upon him as having the luster of a lotus leaf;
one should place the syllable *Oṃ* as Pradyumna on the western petal and meditate upon him as yellow in color.
One should place the syllable *a*, which is Aniruddha, upon the northern petal and meditate upon it as being black in color.
On the petal in the northeast, one should place Brahmā with the syllable "tat" and meditate upon him as having the luster of a lotus petal.
One should meditate on [it] as equal to ten million suns.
One should place Varāha on the petal in the northwest and meditate upon him as being like crushed collyrium.
At the eastern gate, one should place these syllables—Oṃ, Keṃ, Ṭeṃ, Yeṃ—as Vainateya.
And one should meditate upon [him] as being golden in color.
At the southern gate, one should place the Sudarśana, the wheel of the chariot of splendor consisting of three spokes;
one should meditate upon it as having a diamond navel, a thousand spokes, and a radiance equal to ten million suns.
One should place the Śārṅga bow at the western gate;
one should meditate upon it as resembling Indra’s rainbow.
One should install Aniruddha at the northern door with the syllables *sveṃ*, *ṭheṃ*, *heṃ*,
and *theṃ*, and meditate upon him as being of all colors.
One should install the Pāñcajanya conch in the intermediate directions with the syllables *veṃ*, *ṇeṃ*, *kṣeṃ*, and *kṣeṃ*.
One should meditate on the one who has the color of the moon.
One should place Gheṃ, Heṃ, Bheṃ, Heṃ, Śrī, and Padma to the right;
one should meditate upon her as white.
One should place Puṣṭi within the lotus with the syllables *geṃ*, *ḍeṃ*, *veṃ*, and *śeṃ*;
one should meditate on her as white.
One should place the Vanamālā in front with *heṃ* and *seṃ*.
One should meditate upon him as having many colors.
Oṃ, one should place Nandaka in the northeast of the citi;
one should meditate upon him as being the color of space.
Saying "Oṃ," one should place the armor (*varman*) in the southeast;
one should meditate upon it as having many colors.
Oṃ kṣeṃ leṃ: one should place the Śrīvatsa [mark] and meditate upon it as white.
Oṃ cheṃ ṭheṃ: one should place the Kaustubha gem in the northwest and meditate upon the radiant Āditya.

Then, one should place the lords of the directions—Śakra and Agni, Yama and Nairṛta, Varuṇa, Pavana, Kubera, and Īśāna—in their respective external positions within the maṇḍala, using the syllables Oṃ and Auṃ;

Health, the increase of wealth and grain, the destruction of enemies, and subjugation—whatever man constantly worships the God according to this rite, he generates prosperity; or, if that does not please him, then having reached Śvetadvīpa and pierced the solar orb, he attains Pradyumna and Saṃkarṣaṇa, and having attained the state of a supreme deity, he reaches the state of being partless (niṣkala).

To him whose body illuminates the expanse of the sky colored by the twilight, shining with stars in the form of rows of teeth as pure as the peaks of mountains visible from every direction; to him whose broad, rounded, and beautiful conch-like neck is firmly established in the middle of the mountain-peak of his shoulders, where the mind is joined with the steady tip of the creeper-like tongue flickering on the palate; to him whose great chest is adorned and marked with the Śrīvatsa; and to him who wears long hanging garlands woven from various beautiful, most fragrant loose flowers.

To him whose arms, forearms, palms, and claws are raised high and uplifted by the power of his conquest over the movements of the Maruts and Ādityas, serving as fierce and terrible weapons; who possesses the extremely sharp thunderbolt-weapon for drinking the blood of Hiraṇyakaśipu; whose waist-girth is bound with a supreme yellow silk garment; who is the Great Being, the divine Narasiṃha and others, with a waist, thighs, knees, and joints that are firm, compact, elevated, long-lasting, and well-knit; who is endowed with steady sinews; whose ankles and joints are hidden by a slender body extended as befits his devotees; and who possesses great speed and velocity through the force of his mighty arms.

O Blessed One, homage to you! You cause the surface of the earth to tremble by the power of the stride of your feet; you possess the shade of the Śrīvṛkṣa, conch, discus, mace, āsana, nandyāvarta, banner, goad, parasol, mirror, fish, tortoise, waves, garland, moon, sun, bull, horse, elephant, chariot, the Supreme Person, and the most auspicious hair-pores; your gracious feet, which face [all beings], are worshipped by inconceivable hosts such as the Mahendra, Vasu, Rudra, Āditya, Sādhyā, Aśvin, and Marut gaṇas; O Blessed One, homage to you! Come, come!

O Blessed One, endowed with the greatness of the attributes of self-power, heroism, splendor, and personal valor, and manifested through the purity of Sāṃkhya, Yoga, and the inner self; arise, O Supreme God, shaking all your limbs and wiping away all sins! For the destruction of those possessed by Vipranāśa, O Supreme Person, O Most Auspicious One, O Lover of Devotees, grant fearlessness for the sake of favoring your devotees; may the Blessed One explain that Brahman, which is truth, beginningless, unsurpassed, and the supreme liberation.

May the Blessed One know this; having cast away evil, having cast away defilement, lead me ever to peace, lead me to the highest good, lead me to well-being, lead me to blessings. I take refuge in You, O Viṣṇu, O Blessed One, O Lotus-eyed One, O Supreme Person whose nature consists of the qualities of knowledge, sovereignty, power, strength, and splendor; O Most Auspicious One, Padmanābha, Hayashiras, Ādivarāha, Narasiṃha, Vāmana, Trivikrama, Rāma, Rāma, Vāsudeva, Saṅkarṣaṇa, Pradyumna, Aniruddha, O Puruṣa!

O Vāsudeva, whose deeds from beginning to middle to end are true, whose essence is action, who possesses the illusion of day and night, who wears crimson and white garments, who has the eagle, the palm tree, and the dolphin as his banners, and whose navel is supreme ignorance, karma, and time—may there be well-being for us, may there be well-being for our progeny!
You alone are the mantra, you are the protection, and you are the unsurpassed medicine.
O Lord of the World, do not impel this world toward even the threefold suffering.
O Viṣṇu, you who are affectionate toward those who have come for refuge, I take refuge in you, O Brahman.
Then, the one of great intelligence becomes pure, having emerged from the suffering of existence. || 2 ||
Thus was he addressed, O king of kings, by the seer endowed with divine vision.
Having paid homage at the feet of the sage, together with his attendants and the kings.
Having performed a circumambulation, he entered his own city.
Those sages, too, were permitted by the wise Mārkaṇḍeya.
Having paid homage to the god Hari, they then departed for their own hermitages.
King Vajra, whose soul was devoted to dharma, [listened] to what was spoken by Mārkaṇḍeya.
Constantly reflecting upon the Purāṇa, he was entirely devoted to Nārāyaṇa.
And they constantly enjoyed their sovereignty, protecting the subjects in accordance with righteousness.

Thus ends the three hundred and fifty-fifth chapter, titled "The Description of the Hymn to Śrī Narasiṃha," in the third section of the *Śrī Viṣṇudharmottara*, within the second part of the *Śrī Viṣṇu Mahāpurāṇa*, in the dialogue between Mārkaṇḍeya and Vajra. || 355 ||
Thus ends the glorious Viṣṇudharmottara.
And thus ends this Viṣṇu Mahāpurāṇa.
